en.h1: RepoTracker – Track Northern Lights in Real Time

helpPopup.title: How to use RepoTracker
helpPopup.text:
Click anywhere on the map to see the aurora forecast for that location.
Use the 📍 button to check your current position.

Note: Cloud cover can affect visibility even if aurora activity is strong.

questions.q: Mitä ovat aurinkotuuli ja IMF Bz?
questions.a: Aurinkotuuli tuo energiaa Maan magneettikenttään. IMF Bz-arvo kertoo kentän suunnan – negatiivinen Bz lisää revontulien todennäköisyyttä.
Pukeudu lämpimästi kerroksittain. Käytä talvitakkia, lämpimiä kenkiä ja varavaatteita. Älä aja huonosti auratuilla teillä.

faq.pageTitle: Northern Lights FAQ – Frequently asked questions
faq.title: Frequently asked questions about the northern lights

questions.q: When is the best time to see the Northern Lights?
questions.a: The Northern Lights are best seen on dark, clear nights in autumn and spring. The best time is between 9 p.m. and 2 a.m.

questions.q: What do the values on the map mean?
questions.a: The Kp index indicates geomagnetic activity. The higher the value, the more likely auroras will be visible.

questions.q: How does cloud cover affect visibility?
questions.a: Clouds block the Northern Lights. Check the cloud cover map before you go – clear skies are essential.

questions.q: Do I need a dark place?
questions.a: Yes. Light pollution reduces visibility. Move away from street lights and choose an open area.

questions.q: Can the Northern Lights be seen in southern Finland?
questions.a: Yes, but less frequently. A high Kp index (≥ 5–6) and clear skies are required.

questions.q: How do I know when the Northern Lights will appear?
questions.a: Use real-time maps like RepoTracker.fi and follow NOAA and Finnish Meteorological Institute updates.

questions.q: What are solar wind and IMF Bz?
questions.a: Solar wind brings energy to Earth's magnetic field. A negative IMF Bz increases aurora chances.

questions.q: What should you keep in mind when going hunting for the Northern Lights?
questions.a: Dress warmly in layers. Wear winter boots and gloves, and avoid poorly maintained roads.
